title: Give OLY-B-S3-01 a lab run-config mechanism and test
summary: Add a small athena-core lab module that parses and validates a recorded lab configuration (all three systems, a task, a pinned commit and a positive spend cap each), refuses a run once its cap is spent, and gives each run a config fingerprint. Record it as the mechanism of OLY-B-S3-01 in docs/spec.toml with a "status: not shown" measure naming the test that shows it.

defaults_applied.how: New module has tests; fmt, clippy and test criteria included.
Criteria run the validator and cap check rather than checking that files exist.
One focused module plus its test and spec entry.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal and audience: the owner and the verifier judge whether OLY-B-S3-01 has a real, tested mechanism; the lab config is what a later operator uses to run the three studied systems.

Code survey: read docs/spec.toml (the OLY-B-S3-01 entry at line ~2961 has mechanism = "none" and measure "The spec gap list; status: requirement"), crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs (pattern for a spec-entry test: finds the entry, rejects mechanism none, checks owner and measure ending), crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (status labels such as keep rule, repeated, mistakes), and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (Config::parse and validate, whose refusal pattern the lab config follows). Entry point is a new crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs: parse, then validate, then check the cap before each run. No record or data file under crates/ is added, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are untouched; the lab config is read from a caller-supplied TOML string, not stored as a record. The property is measured directly by calling the validator and the cap check, not a stand-in.

Existing code: docs/spec.toml, crates/athena-core/tests/model_roster.rs (test pattern reused), crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (validation style extended by analogy). No existing spend-cap or lab code was found by grep in crates/.
The measure is 'status: not shown' because no `athena status` label measures lab runs; the measure names the test file that shows it.

Buy-first: the config fingerprint uses a hash crate already in Cargo.lock if one exists, otherwise std's stable hashing is avoided and a documented existing dependency is reused; no new heavy crate is added. toml and serde are already used by the workspace.
Environment: none; no CI workflow, push or history read is needed. This adds a refusal rule only for new lab configs, not for past job readings, so no replay refusal-rate criterion applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-S3-01 no longer has mechanism = "none"; its mechanism names crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs, owner stays "Athena", and its measure ends with `status: not shown` and names the test file crates/athena-core/tests/lab_runs.rs.

crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs exists, is exported from crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs, and defines a lab configuration with the three systems, a task, a pinned commit and a spend cap in USD per system, plus a fingerprint of the configuration.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test lab_runs`: a valid config with three systems and positive caps is accepted; configs missing a system, with a zero or negative cap, or without a pinned commit are refused; a run whose recorded spend reaches its cap is refused; the same config gives the same fingerprint and a changed cap gives a different one.

The test lab_runs.rs also reads docs/spec.toml and fails if the OLY-B-S3-01 entry has mechanism none, no owner, or a measure not ending in a status label; it fails when lab.rs's validation is removed and passes with it.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` as separate commands (or the recorded Athena checks on the final tree); all pass.
CHANGELOG.md gains an entry for this job; no existing entry of docs/decisions.md or records/ is edited.

out_of_scope: Actually running the three studied systems or spending money on them.
Changing other requirements in docs/spec.toml, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
